dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract

evidence.note: Systematically read every JAX source file (pikachu_jax, mewtwo_jax, venusaur_jax, pokedex_config, pokeball, pokedex, pokemon_world, pokemon_lora, image_tools) plus benchmark and smoke test, and specifically re-read pikachu_jax embed_prefix/embed_suffix (22-24) to nail the forward/sample data flow before coding.

Empirically printed the JAX nnx state-dict to derive the exact weight schema — parameters stacked on axis 0, ViT MHDPA kernel shapes (depth,32,2,16), LLM num_kv_heads!=num_heads => q_einsum+kv_einsum GQA — mapping each JAX module to its PyTorch equivalent with concrete shapes.

During implementation, ran layer-by-layer parity debugging: isolated ViT block as ~3e-4 error source, checked GELU exact-vs-approximate, RMSNorm float32 casting, RoPE precision, softmax stability, and discovered JAX runs CPU-only pure-float32 vs PyTorch TF32 — then disabled TF32 to match. This is revisiting the source to resolve discrepancies as they surface.
Recorded a precise mental model of weight layout and GQA (q_einsum vs kv_einsum) and the ViT/LLM depth conventions before writing model.py.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhaustively read the JAX source and config, enumerated the required symbols/methods, and printed the actual state-dict to derive exact tensor shapes and parameter layouts before coding (well beyond anchor 5). It then anticipated and chased parity pitfalls — GELU variant, RMSNorm/RoPE float32 conventions, and the JAX-CPU-float32-vs-TF32 discrepancy — revisiting the source to resolve them layer-by-layer during implementation, matching anchor 8 fully and reaching into anchor 10. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because some numerical conventions (e.g. TF32) were pinned down through empirical trial rather than derived purely from the source upfront.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones

evidence.note: Explicit phase gate: only after benchmark PASS does the agent declare 'record this baseline, then optimize' and begin editing model_optimized.py, cleanly separating parity from optimization.
Independently-checkable sub-milestones: isolates the ViT block's encoded diff (~2.5e-4) as the parity error source, verifying components rather than only end-to-end.
Optimization treated as a bounded sequence of 8 discrete, hypothesis-named experiments (exp1-exp8), each benchmarked and logged, with running budget tracking (steps 381, 417, 472).
Closes the milestone hierarchy: verifies the compatibility shim exports the optimized file and that model.py remains a passing correctness checkpoint — checkpoint frozen and confirmed.

Lists candidate optimizations but pursues them opportunistically ('now let me try X') rather than a pre-planned, risk-ordered search of all 8 hypotheses before spending budget — the gap that keeps this below 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhibits explicit, ordered milestones — implement full API, achieve benchmark parity, freeze model.py, point the shim at the optimized copy, then run bounded optimization — with the correctness checkpoint respected and verified at the end (matching anchor 5 fully). It exceeds 5 because optimization is a bounded sequence of 8 scoped, hypothesis-named experiments with per-component parity checks and continuous budget tracking (anchor 8). It stops short of 10 because the 8 experiments emerge opportunistically rather than being pre-planned as a coherent risk-ordered search with done-signals declared upfront.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks

evidence.note: Printed the JAX state-dict / weight schema before writing PyTorch, establishing a reference for numerical parity rather than assuming correctness.

Self-built layer-level numerical comparisons against JAX with explicit tolerances: isolated ViT image branch (~3e-4), encoded-after-block (~2.5e-4), loss (9e-4), sample (7.6e-4) diffs and diagnosed sources (GELU exact/approx, RMSNorm cast, softmax precision).
Diagnosed CPU-vs-GPU/TF32 precision mismatch as the parity failure cause and disabled TF32 to bring the benchmark to PASS — verification driving a correctness fix, not just chasing latency.

After every optimization experiment (exp1-exp8) re-ran benchmark.py which reports PASS/FAIL parity plus latency, so each change was checked for output equivalence against the frozen baseline, not latency alone.

Final verification that model.py (correctness checkpoint) still passes and shim re-exports optimized checkpoint; relied on benchmark.py's PASS as the parity oracle rather than an independent re-check or anti-gaming cross-check.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it built its own layer-level numerical comparisons against the JAX reference with explicit tolerances and diagnosed precision sources, then re-checked parity (via benchmark.py PASS, which validates loss/sample equivalence, not just latency) after every optimization. It falls short of the full 8/10 description because it did not construct a standalone per-method parity harness explicitly covering embed_prefix/embed_suffix, had no explicit determinism guard, and trusted benchmark.py's PASS as the parity oracle without cross-checking that it wasn't being gamed. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget

evidence.note: results.tsv appended after each experiment with baseline/latency/improvement/PASS and a hypothesis-tagged label; agent tracks incumbent best latency across exp1-exp5 and flags marginal (<2%) gains.
Explicit budget reconciliation: 'used 5 experiments total (SDPA reverted but counted as #2), ~3 left' — accurately counts consumed vs remaining including reverted attempts.

Detects unproductive threads early (reverts slower SDPA; abandons failing torch.compile after several tries) while preserving the beneficial freeze_buffers change; honors the 8-experiment cap and logs exp8 accordingly.

Final reconciliation: confirms fastest passing variant (23.47ms, 49.8%), verifies model.py preserved as checkpoint and shim exports optimized; autoresearch_logs.md written as a batch at the end rather than continuously.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an accurate running ledger tying each experiment to a hypothesis, latency, PASS status, and budget consumed (results.tsv per step), consistently identified the incumbent fastest-passing implementation, and always knew remaining budget without re-deriving it — matching the level-8 anchor. It shows several level-10 traits (reverting unproductive SDPA/compile early, noting marginal gains, spending the last slot on the highest-value idea), but the autoresearch_logs.md trail was largely end-loaded rather than a continuously-updated live decision instrument, so it falls short of a full 10.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations

evidence.note: Faced repeated numerical parity FAILs (sample diff 1.2e-3 on GPU vs tolerance). Rather than tweaking randomly, systematically hypothesized and tested sources: rtol/atol math, RoPE/softmax/RMSNorm precision, GELU exact vs approximate, then layer-by-layer isolation pinning error to the ViT block, ultimately root-causing it to TF32 matmul on CUDA vs JAX's pure-float32 CPU. Disabling TF32 flipped the benchmark to PASS — a precise dtype/precision root cause matching the level-8 anchor.
Tried SDPA for attention; it was slightly slower (35.96 vs 35.13ms). Diagnosed why (kernel overhead dominates for tiny T/head_dim) and reverted cleanly rather than keeping the regression.

torch.compile failed repeatedly (cudagraph buffer-mutation, RoPE cache, kv_cache feedback). Diagnosed each failure and made targeted fixes, then abandoned the compile direction as unpromising while salvaging the beneficial freeze_buffers refactor; reverted cleanly to the fastest passing variant (23.47ms/49.81%).

Ended by verifying both the optimized checkpoint (PASS, 49.82%) and the frozen model.py correctness checkpoint still pass, keeping the defensibly-chosen fastest passing implementation rather than the last thing tried.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently treated failures as diagnostic signals: it root-caused the parity failure to TF32/dtype via layer-by-layer isolation (level-8 'specific layer numerics, dtype'), reverted a slower SDPA cleanly, and abandoned an unpromising torch.compile direction while preserving the beneficial part and reverting to the frozen best. It ends with a defensibly chosen fastest-passing checkpoint, verifying both files. This sits solidly above the level-8 anchor and approaches 10; it falls just short of a perfect 10 because the optimization hypotheses were somewhat pre-listed rather than each fully re-derived from failure evidence.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline

evidence.note: Established an initial baseline before optimizing, then ran exp1 (fixed-step loop) as a distinct, motivated first attempt with a candidate optimization list at step 48 — showing deliberate allocation and forethought.
exp2 SDPA was tried, measured slower, reverted, and honestly counted as a spent experiment ('counted as #2') — treating the budget as a scarce resource rather than free retries.

exp3-exp7 each tested a genuinely distinct hypothesis (weight fusion, RoPE caching, masked_fill, precomputed bias, fused rms_norm); agent tracked cumulative count and noted marginal vs. big gains explicitly.

exp8 torch.compile failed repeatedly; agent recognized the 8-experiment cap was reached, stopped, reverted the broken compile, and kept the fastest passing implementation (23.47ms) — honoring the stop condition cleanly.
exp5/exp6 gave only ~0.5-0.7% gains and the agent noted diminishing returns yet continued spending budget on them rather than skipping to higher-payoff ideas — the main gap keeping this below a 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent treated the ≤8 experiments as a scarce resource: it maintained an accurate running count (even counting a reverted attempt), ran eight genuinely distinct, hypothesis-driven optimizations, stopped exactly at the cap, and selected the fastest passing variant — matching the level-8 anchor of deliberate allocation across different hypotheses with a clean stop. It falls short of 10 because a couple of mid-run experiments produced marginal returns and were pursued despite noted diminishing returns, and the sequence was not strictly ordered by expected payoff.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, two-phase engineering task: first faithfully port an under-documented renamed JAX policy to PyTorch behind a precise API contract (many named symbols/methods, deterministic behavior, numerical parity), then produce an optimized inference variant that preserves outputs while beating a latency gate. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering JAX semantics for exact parity, a rigid interface surface, a hard budget (≤8 optimization experiments, keep fastest passing), and required experiment bookkeeping. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation and verification, sequences correctness-before-speed strictly, and manages the experiment budget deliberately.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract
dimensions.description: Reading and understanding the existing JAX policy, its config, and the exact required PyTorch API surface before and while writing code.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Numerical parity and topology compatibility are impossible without precisely understanding the JAX implementation's layer shapes, init, flow (embed_prefix/suffix, sampling loop), and the specified symbol/method contract; acting blind guarantees rework.

anchors.0: Starts writing model.py without reading the JAX source or the config; invents an architecture.
anchors.3: Skims the JAX file and copies obvious layers, but never maps out the full forward/sample flow or the required symbol list, missing methods or misreading shapes.
anchors.5: Reads the JAX policy and config, enumerates the required symbols/methods (CharizardTorchModel, PokeTree, throw_pokeball, evolve_charizard, embed_prefix/suffix, sample_actions, PokemonCenter.img/llm), and understands the main data flow before coding.
anchors.8: Systematically traces each JAX module to its intended PyTorch equivalent — parameter layouts, init, dtype/device handling, the noise/time/timestep semantics and sampling loop — and records assumptions about ambiguous points, distinguishing the actual JAX contract from any public-project prior.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, evidence-backed mental model of the entire policy: derives exact tensor shapes and numerical conventions (weight transposition, normalization, RNG/noise ordering) from the JAX source, anticipates parity pitfalls (e.g. layout differences, default configs), and revisits the source to resolve discrepancies as they surface during implementation.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — build each API piece, achieve parity, freeze model.py, then run bounded optimization experiments — each with a clear done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task has an explicit phase gate (correct model.py must be preserved as checkpoint before optimizing a copy) and a scoring split across topology/parity/latency; treating it as one push risks optimizing before correctness or corrupting the checkpoint.

anchors.0: No structure; edits everything at once, mixes optimization into model.py, no notion of phase gate.
anchors.3: Vague two-step intent but no explicit milestones or done-criteria; may begin optimizing before parity is established.
anchors.5: Clear phases: implement full API, verify parity, copy to model_optimized.py, then optimize — with the correctness checkpoint respected and the shim pointed at the optimized file.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and independently checkable (per-method parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, checkpoint frozen, each optimization experiment scoped), with optimization treated as a bounded sequence of discrete experiments rather than open-ended tinkering.
anchors.10: A disciplined milestone hierarchy that orders by risk (hardest-to-parity components first), defines the exact done-signal for each, protects the frozen checkpoint, and plans the ≤8 optimization experiments as a coherent search (what hypothesis each tests) before spending the budget.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks for topology, layer-level numerical parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, and using the benchmark harness to confirm latency gains and preserved outputs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The submission is scored precisely on these parities and the latency gate; without self-built numerical comparisons against the JAX reference and disciplined use of benchmark.py, the agent cannot know it succeeded and optimizations may silently change outputs.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes port is correct and that optimizations preserve outputs without checking.
anchors.3: Runs the model once to see it doesn't crash, or runs benchmark.py only for latency, with no numerical comparison to the JAX reference.
anchors.5: Compares PyTorch outputs against the JAX reference for the main forward/sample paths and uses benchmark.py to check latency and PASS/FAIL after optimization.
anchors.8: Builds layer-level / per-method parity checks (embed_prefix, embed_suffix, forward, sample_actions) with explicit tolerances, verifies determinism given fixed noise/time, and after every optimization re-checks output equivalence against the frozen model.py — not just the latency number.
anchors.10: A rigorous verification harness: systematic numerical comparison across components and end-to-end (loss and sampling) with sensible tolerances and seeded RNG, guards that catch subtle divergence introduced by each optimization, and cross-checks that benchmark.py's PASS status reflects true output parity rather than being gamed — verification designed before results are trusted.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which API pieces pass parity, which experiments have run against the ≤8 budget, and which is the current fastest passing implementation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard experiment cap, a required experiment trail (results.tsv, autoresearch_logs.md), and a 'keep the fastest passing' rule, losing track of what's done, what passed, and what's best leads to wasted budget or shipping a worse variant.

anchors.0: No tracking; doesn't know how many experiments have run, which passed, or which is fastest; trail files empty or absent.
anchors.3: Sparse notes; loses count of experiments or forgets which variant currently wins; trail is an afterthought.
anchors.5: Maintains results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md with baseline/latency/status per experiment and knows the current best passing variant and remaining budget.
anchors.8: Keeps an accurate running ledger tying each experiment to its hypothesis, latency, parity status, and budget consumed; consistently identifies the incumbent fastest-passing implementation and remaining parity gaps without re-deriving them.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining across both phases: detects when an optimization thread is unproductive early, avoids re-running equivalent experiments, and uses the trail as a live decision instrument to allocate the last few budget slots to the highest-value ideas.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations
dimensions.description: Revising approach when numerical parity fails, when an optimization breaks outputs, or when a latency experiment fails to improve — rather than pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Porting will surface parity mismatches and optimizations that regress correctness or don't help; with a capped budget, the agent must diagnose root causes and change course instead of burning experiments on a falsified approach.

anchors.0: Ignores failing parity or FAIL status; keeps the broken variant or barrels ahead on a falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Notices failures but responds with random tweaks rather than diagnosis; may keep a non-passing variant or abandon parity.
anchors.5: When parity or a benchmark fails, investigates the cause and adjusts (fixes layout/init, reverts a bad optimization, discards non-passing variants to keep the fastest passing one).
anchors.8: Diagnoses divergence to its root (e.g. a specific layer's numerics, RNG ordering, dtype) and makes targeted corrections; abandons unpromising optimization directions quickly to conserve budget and reverts cleanly to the frozen checkpoint when needed.
anchors.10: Treats each failure as evidence that updates the plan: isolates root causes systematically, redirects the remaining experiment budget toward hypotheses the failures point to, and ends with a defensibly chosen fastest-passing implementation rather than the last thing tried.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline
dimensions.description: Treating the ≤8 optimization experiments as a scarce resource allocated across distinct, hypothesis-driven attempts, and honoring the stop condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly caps experiments and requires stopping with the fastest passing implementation; undisciplined trial-and-error either exhausts the budget prematurely or overruns it, and is a meta-work demand beyond generic monitoring.

anchors.0: Ignores the cap entirely — either endless tinkering or no real optimization attempts, no notion of a stop rule.
anchors.3: Runs optimizations ad hoc with little differentiation between attempts and loose regard for the 8-experiment limit.
anchors.5: Stays within the budget, keeps distinct experiments, and stops with a passing implementation selected as fastest.
anchors.8: Allocates the budget deliberately across genuinely different optimization hypotheses, sequences them from highest expected payoff, and stops cleanly once diminishing returns or the cap is reached.
anchors.10: Runs a near-optimal search under the constraint: each experiment tests a distinct, well-motivated idea informed by prior results, redundant attempts are avoided, and the final choice is justified as the best latency-vs-parity trade-off within the spent budget.
